title: lint_test_isolation.py T010 BLOCKER count is 217 across 127 files, far above ISS-0121/GH#387+#402's reported '<10' — baseline suppression file is stale (dated 2026-05-29, 524 entries) and no longer matches current line numbers/content
scope: tests/integration/*.zig (127 files scanned, 217 BLOCKER + 25 MAJOR findings). Discovered while re-running zig build test-env-verify's C5 check after fixing ISS-0139's single-file adp03 violation and seeing C5 immediately fail again on a DIFFERENT file (adp04_user_tenant_binding_test.zig). Unrelated to ISS-0139/ISS-0140 (GH #442/#443), which are scoped to the tenant-schema-drift issue and its single-file T010 companion finding.
symptom: `python tools/lint_test_isolation.py tests/integration` reports `127 file(s) checked. BLOCKER=217 MAJOR=25 MINOR=0`, with `tools/lint_test_isolation.baseline.json` suppressing 24 additional known findings. This means `zig build test-env-verify` check C5 can never report HEALTHY on this codebase in its current state -- fixing one file (as ISS-0139 did for adp03_tenant_context_resolution_test.zig) simply surfaces the linter's next unsuppressed finding, since the check only prints the FIRST blocking violation it hits rather than the full count.
reproduction: python tools/lint_test_isolation.py tests/integration    (or) zig build test-env-verify, check C5
root_cause_analysis: GH #387 (ISS-0121) and its follow-up GH #402 claimed to drive T010 hardcoded-UUID MAJOR findings from 174 down to <10 across the integration suite (per CHANGELOG.md's ISS-0138 entry cross-reference and gh issue title for #402). However: (1) tools/lint_test_isolation.baseline.json -- the suppression file that lets already-known legacy findings not block the gate -- is dated 2026-05-29T16:26:29Z, predating both #387's and #402's work, and contains 524 entries matched by exact (file, line, message) key; any file edited since baseline generation (including by unrelated changes that shift line numbers) silently drops out of suppression and reappears as a fresh BLOCKER even though the underlying finding was already known/accepted at the time. (2) It is not yet established whether the reported '<10' figure in #402 was measured with or without --no-baseline, or whether large amounts of new test code were added after #402 closed without following the per-test-UUID convention. Both mechanisms would produce exactly today's symptom: a linter that reports 217 current BLOCKERs despite an issue history claiming near-zero.
acceptance_criteria: Determine why the current BLOCKER count (217) is so much higher than #402's reported outcome (<10) -- stale baseline, severity reclassification, new unconvention-following code, or some combination

Either regenerate tools/lint_test_isolation.baseline.json against current tests/integration/ content (if the 217 findings are legacy/already-accepted), or file per-file/per-cluster follow-up issues and fix them (if they are genuine new violations)
zig build test-env-verify check C5 passes cleanly (BLOCKER=0) OR the baseline is regenerated to correctly suppress all currently-known legacy findings
Document in this issue (or a follow-up) whether a CI step should regenerate/validate the baseline automatically so it cannot silently go stale again
evidence_file: N/A -- see symptom field for exact lint output; full BLOCKER list available via `python tools/lint_test_isolation.py tests/integration`
resolution: Diagnosed as (b): a mix of (mostly) baseline line-number drift and (a smaller number of) genuinely new violations, NOT primarily new unconvention-following code. Diffed the current `--no-baseline --json` scan (266 findings: 217 BLOCKER + 49 MAJOR) against the 2026-05-29 baseline's 524 entries by (file, code, message) -- ignoring line number, since UUID literals are stable text even when surrounding edits shift line numbers. 218 of 266 findings (82%) matched an existing baseline entry exactly except for line number: legitimate baseline maintenance, not new violations. Only 48 were genuinely new (37 BLOCKER + 11 MAJOR) across 21 files. Fixed 41 of those 48 in source by replacing hardcoded UUID literals with per-test-generated values (TestHarness.newUuidString/newUuid, bpm.uuid.generateUuidV4BytesInto/newUuidV4, or the file's own existing fillRandom helper, following the exact pattern in adp03_tenant_context_resolution_test.zig), removed one genuine module-level shared-counter T020 violation (entity_subsystem_test.zig's global_test_counter, replaced with a per-call random suffix), converted one never-mutated module var to const (onboarding_realm_guard_test.zig's dummy_ctx_byte), and added explicit BPM_TEST_DB_URL doc-comment mentions to 5 files that use TestHarness (which reads the var internally) without literally naming it, satisfying T050 honestly. 7 of the 48 were triaged as legitimate non-fixes and added to the regenerated baseline rather than force-fixed: env01_test.zig:129 and tm01_tenant_list_test.zig:45/57 are in-memory AuthContext.user_id actor markers never persisted as DB rows (same accepted pattern as several already-baselined files); env01_test.zig:463 is a deliberate non-null sentinel for a negative validation test that executeSaga() rejects before any DB write; helpers.zig:344/349/350 are an atomically-synchronized, well-documented process-local cache in the shared test-harness infrastructure file (not a test block itself), the same class as the already-baselined helpers.zig:34 `names` var. Regenerated tools/lint_test_isolation.baseline.json (225 entries, version 2) against current file/line state via `python tools/lint_test_isolation.py --no-baseline --json tests/integration` -- every remaining raw-scan finding is either a legitimate baseline-line-number restatement or one of the 7 explicitly-triaged exceptions above; no genuinely-new violation was suppressed. Verified: `python tools/lint_test_isolation.py tests/integration` now exits 0 (BLOCKER=0, MAJOR=0, 225 suppressed). `zig build test-env-verify` C5 (test isolation lint) now PASSES. `zig build` and `zig build test` both exit 0 with no 'error set' output. `python3 tools/lint_sql_param_types.py src tests` exits 0. Also found and fixed, in the same session (Unblock-Everything): a `zig build test-env-verify` C4 (schema baseline) failure caused by 2 leaked `public.tenant` rows (storage_mode='SCHEMA', no matching Postgres schema) from an unrelated earlier test run predating this session -- deleted. Also discovered, while verifying the fix with `zig build test-integration`, a large pre-existing and unrelated pattern of non-deterministic test failures across the whole integration suite when run concurrently (confirmed pre-existing via an isolated A/B comparison against the unmodified main-branch svc01/svc03 test files) -- filed separately as ISS-0144 / GitHub #454 per the No Issue Left Local-Only directive, not fixed in this session (out of scope: a much larger cross-binary concurrency/schema-provisioning investigation, unrelated to the T010 lint-baseline work).
